name: 4130 chromoly normalized
note: MIL-T-6736B (3 May 1965) Table II, condition (N) normalized or stress relieved: 95,000 psi UTS and 75,000 psi yield minimum for walls up to 0.035 in incl. (10%) and over 0.035 to 0.187 in incl. (12%); over 0.187 in is 90,000/70,000 (everyspec copy at meracing.com/UserFiles/Products/Tubes/MIL-T-6736B_2.pdf, read 2026-09-24). Retail aircraft 4130 tube (e.g. Aircraft Spruce condition N) is sold to MIL-T-6736 / its successor AMS-T-6736, whose current table was not checked. Replaces 483 (AMS 6371 cold-drawn tube, 70 ksi, Aircraft Materials), which was a different condition

name: 4130 chromoly heat-treated

name: Magnesium AZ31B tube
note: ASTM B107 AZ31B-F tube minimum 16 ksi (low end of 110-140 range read from B107); compressive yield 12 ksi (83 MPa) typical against 24 ksi (165 MPa) tensile yield typical, BTI AZ31B tube page, so bending onset is lower (footnote in tables.md)

alts.label: the ~83 MPa typical compressive yield instead

footnote: Bending yields the compression face first, and AZ31B tube is much weaker in compression: BTI lists 83 MPa (12 ksi) compressive yield against 165 MPa tensile, both typical. The row uses the ASTM B107 tensile minimum, so it overstates the load before a permanent bend by about 1.3x. The figures that follow mix a typical compressive value with the minimum-based rows; no compressive minimum was found.
